Running and recent sessions show up here.
Keeps the device in the bar; only excludes it from the All feed.

Connect Telegram, Lark, or WeChat to get notified and chat with your agents.

Open WeChat, tap the \"+\" and choose Scan, then point your camera at the code.

Enable an agent to manage its skills.

Create a skill to guide this agent.

Links this expert into the selected agents\' skills.
The accent tints buttons, links, and live indicators.
A native Android client for the codeg multi-agent coding server.

The language the bot replies in.

How many levels deep agents may delegate.
Tap ▲▼ to reorder the bottom bar; tap a row\'s name to make it the tab the app opens on.
Uncheck a tab to hide it from the bottom bar. Settings always stays visible.
Always visible — it is the way back to this screen
Start with the running/needs-you/online summary row open.
Start with the needs-you card list open.
On the Activity tab, horizontal swipes switch devices (All → each device); swiping past the ends moves between tabs.
Eye = show on this phone only · Switch = on/off on the server (all devices)
Not available — install it on the server to enable.
Uses your Claude subscription login on the server. Model overrides below are optional.
Point Claude Code at a custom Anthropic-compatible endpoint.
Resolve the endpoint and key from a saved model provider.
Signed in with a ChatGPT subscription on the server.
Run `gemini` once on the server to sign in with Google.
Provider and model-catalog editing lives in the Advanced editor below.
This provider uses OAuth — run hermes setup on the desktop to sign in.
Uses the AWS credential chain on the server.
API key is saved to ~/.hermes/.env. Leave blank to keep the stored key.

CodeBuddy authenticates with an API key. Mainland China builds also require the environment set to “China (internal)”; iOA builds use “iOA”. The overseas build leaves it unset. No API key? Run “codebuddy” in a terminal to sign in with your Tencent account.
Saved as CODEBUDDY_BASE_URL and points CodeBuddy at your private endpoint. The region setting is left unset for self-hosted deployments.

`kimi acp` only authenticates with a stored login token and rejects API keys on their own. To use an API key, codeg writes a managed ~/.kimi-code/config.toml provider AND seeds a local gate token so the session opens — inference still runs on your key.
“API key” writes a codeg-managed config.toml provider and seeds a gate token. “Login” clears that and uses a real `kimi login` session (requires a Kimi subscription).
Run `kimi login` in a terminal to sign in with a Kimi subscription account (device-code OAuth). codeg stores nothing and reuses Kimi’s own login. Saving here removes codeg’s API-key gate token.
The provider protocol Kimi speaks (config.toml `type`). Use Kimi / Moonshot for a Moonshot / platform.kimi.com key.
International = api.moonshot.ai; China (platform.kimi.com keys) = api.moonshot.cn. Custom points at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
Leave blank to use the provider SDK default.
Written to ~/.kimi-code/config.toml and used for inference. From platform.kimi.com or platform.kimi.ai.
Where the API key is written inside config.toml.
Vertex AI uses Google Application Default Credentials — run `gcloud auth application-default login` (no API key).
The model id to use. Tap Fetch to list the models your key can access (e.g. kimi-k2.7-code) — avoids “model not found” errors.
Tokens, e.g. 262144. Leave blank to use the model default.
Written verbatim (comments preserved) and validated as TOML. codeg also seeds the gate token so the session opens.
Authenticated via a Kimi account login.
Authenticated via API key (codeg seeded the local gate token).
Not authenticated yet — save an API key below (or sign in) to open Kimi sessions.
Enter a model id (Kimi requires one for API-key mode).
Enter an API key and endpoint first
Key works, but no models were returned
Couldn’t list models — check the key and endpoint
Choose which pi binary runs. Use the default, or point at your own pi build.
Use the bundled pi-acp adapter with the pi on your PATH. Install pi with: npm install -g @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent
Run your own pi build, install, or wrapper.
An absolute path, a command name on PATH, or a wrapper script (e.g. a monorepo ./pi-test.sh).
With a custom config directory, the Skills, Experts, and Office tools managed in Settings won’t apply to this pi — manage its skills in that folder directly.
Custom pi flags (--approve, -e, …) aren’t forwarded by pi-acp — wrap pi in a script and point the command at it.
Enter a pi command to save
Pi authenticates with your model provider’s API key. The key is written to ~/.pi/agent/auth.json and the model selection to settings.json.
Defines a provider in ~/.pi/agent/models.json at your endpoint. Most self-hosted or proxy servers use openai-completions.
Stored in ~/.pi/agent/auth.json for the selected provider.
Saved for this provider — leave blank to keep the stored key.
When codeg connects pi to a folder, mark that folder trusted so pi loads the project’s local config and skills without a separate prompt.
Only folders you open here are trusted, never your whole machine — and this affects config loading only, not what pi is allowed to run.
The controls below merge into ~/.grok/config.toml, preserving your other keys and comments. Other keys stay editable under Advanced.
Saved as XAI_API_KEY for this agent, or run “grok login” in a terminal for subscription sign-in (SuperGrok / X Premium+).
Approve to start building, or send notes to have the plan revised.
The agent didn\'t include a plan.
The turn ended before your notes could be sent.
Both methods sign in to Cursor\'s own backend — cursor-agent has no custom-endpoint support, so there is no API URL to set.
Sign in with your Cursor account in a terminal. No credential is stored here.
A Cursor Dashboard account key for headless or server machines — an alternative to signing in. Not a third-party or OpenAI key.
Run this on the machine hosting codeg, then refresh:
Create one in the Cursor Dashboard under Integrations.
Passed to cursor-agent as its --model flag. Leave unset to use the account default.
Rules and sandbox merge into ~/.cursor/cli-config.json, preserving keys the Cursor CLI wrote. Running sessions pick them up after a restart.
Cursor runs commands without asking. Deny rules below still apply.
Rule syntax: Shell(cmd), Read(path/glob), Write(path/glob), WebFetch(domain), Mcp(server:tool) — deny always wins.
Enter your Cursor API key, or switch to Official Subscription.
No model providers configured for this agent. Add one in Settings → Model Providers.
Edits here override the fields above on save.
These values are written to the agent\'s environment on the server. Leave a field blank to clear it.
Optional model override (QODER_MODEL). Leave blank to use the CLI default.
Written verbatim to Qoder\'s settings file on the server.
ZCode signs in through its own CLI, so there is no API key to store here. Pick the model and approval mode from the session composer once a session is open.
This build doesn\'t know this agent yet, so it can\'t be configured or enabled from the app. Update the app to manage it.
This permanently removes the conversation and its history.
Couldn\'t apply that change. Check your connection and try again.
The session is running a turn. Try again when it finishes.
This agent has no adjustable options.
Options can\'t be changed while the agent is responding.
Folder is fixed for this session
No token for %1$s — add one under Servers first.
Answer below, then submit. You can skip anytime.
The agent wants to proceed with this plan.
The agent needs permission to continue.

resources.string: Discard your changes to %1$s? This can\'t be undone.
Delete %1$s from disk? This can\'t be undone.
Authentication failed. Check your credentials and try again.
Pushing to %1$s needs a token with repo access. It\'s saved as a GitHub account for next time.
Pushing to %1$s requires authentication. Use a personal access token as the password.
Pick documents (Markdown, PRD, Plan…) from the file manager
Added %1$d image(s); %2$d skipped (too large or over the limit)
Attachments exceed the per-message size limit — remove some images and try again
No experts linked to this agent.
No sessions match the current filters.
Couldn\'t load sessions — tap to retry.
This permanently removes the file from the server. There is no trash.
This permanently removes the folder and EVERYTHING inside it from the server. There is no trash.
Someone (or an agent) modified this file after you opened it. Overwriting discards those changes; reloading shows the new content.
The selected folder is outside this workspace
This file is too large to edit on the phone (over 2 MB). Preview still works.
You have unsaved edits to this file.
This agent did not report a context window size.
The session lives on the server; reconnecting only re-attaches this view.
Copies the working directory, title, CLI/Codeg ids and branch — paste into a new session to pick up the context.
%1$s is outside this session\'s working directory.
Available once the session has a working directory.
App-wide text size, on top of the system setting
Quick actions from anywhere; hold the ball 1s and move to reposition it
Assign actions to taps and swipes
Tap a gesture row to change its action. Moving the ball: hold it 1s, then drag — it follows your finger. Swipes fire gestures.
Steps through only the most recent N sessions (running ones first). 1–10, default 5.
The task stops running. It can be requeued on the server later.
The result will be merged into the project branch and the task worktree deleted. This cannot be undone here.
Marks the task done without merging any changes.
The task returns to execution and the agent will redo it per your feedback.
Pushes the work branch and opens a pull request; the task is marked done afterwards. This can take several minutes — the server waits for the PR.
Archived tasks are hidden from the board — toggle \"Show archived\" to find them again.
The task will reappear on the board.
Shelved tasks are filed under Done until you pick them back up.
The task returns to its previous section.
Deletes the task record on the server (worktree kept). This cannot be undone.
No ideas yet — tap + to capture one
Delete the %1$d selected ideas? Their attachment copies are removed too.
Dispatch result unknown — the request may or may not have reached the server
This task\'s submission result is UNKNOWN — it may already exist on the server. Re-dispatching could create a duplicate task. Continue?
Discarding deletes this record. If the task was actually created on the server, it can no longer be tracked from here. Discard?
Scheduled execution is on but no time is picked — tap \"Pick a time\", or turn the switch off to run immediately.
The picked time is already in the past; the task would run immediately. Pick a future time.
It will start running on its device immediately. If it was created elsewhere or has its own schedule, starting it may interrupt that plan.
Batch-start the todo tasks on the targets below — %1$d task(s) across %2$d target(s). Tasks that are scheduled or blocked are skipped automatically.
It will run again on its device.
The task goes back to the To-do column and waits to be started again.
Auto = the project\'s default agent, applied to this task only.
Branch list unavailable — dispatch still uses the project default. Tap the row to retry.
Run \"Check server\" first — re-dispatch unlocks only after the server confirms the task was not created.
Open a session in the project, no worktree
Work task with its own worktree branch
Session mode: after dispatch the session opens automatically and the description below is sent as its first prompt. Branch and schedule don\'t apply.
Description is required in session mode — it becomes the first prompt.
The handoff package carries context only, not code; commit/push/pull via Git yourself.
This session is not synced to a server; handoff unavailable
Migrate server configs between two phones via encrypted text. Fully local — no network, no server calls.
Set a one-time temporary password; the encrypted text is copied to the clipboard. The password is not saved — tell it to the other phone in person.
Encrypted and copied to the clipboard. The clipboard holds ciphertext only, never plaintext tokens; the system or third-party keyboards may retain clipboard content — paste it soon.
Paste the encrypted text exported from the other phone and enter the temporary password to decrypt.
At least 12 characters. Used for this transfer only, never stored. Never reuse a server token as this password.
About to import these servers (for name conflicts, choose whether to overwrite the local config)
Conflicts with local \"%1$s\" — check the box to use the imported config
Security note: the encrypted text contains no plaintext tokens; the clipboard may be retained by the system or keyboards — clear it manually afterwards.
%1$d server(s) skipped at export for missing tokens; their configs are NOT in this ciphertext.
No devices yet — add one in Settings first.
Tasks you create (or dispatch from Ideas) show up here — plus any session you add to the board.
Submitting — waiting for the server receipt.
Pick a device & folder, then jump in
Off: lands in To-do. On: starts immediately and shows in In progress.
Track this session on the board after it is created.
No recent sessions on any device.
Couldn\'t load sessions — tap to retry.
“%2$s” on %1$s is in. Check the task board (or the session) for its live status.
Could not read this agent’s model list; the task will run with its default model.
Tap to pick from the model list
Pick an agent to change the model
Creates a task on the board in todo state — start it there when ready. The draft stays on this device until the target confirms.
Only the board entry goes away — the session itself is untouched.
Delete \"%1$s\"? Tasks already created from it are not affected.
Replace the filled-in title, description and agent with \"%1$s\"?
A template named \"%1$s\" already exists on this device. Replace its content?
Also delete its worktree and working branch
“%1$s” is on the board as a todo — it will not run until you start it.
The device did not confirm the result. Check the dispatch records in the inbox — do not simply resend.
Saving overwrites the title and description on the device; other settings are kept.
What a horizontal swipe does on the Task board: step through the four status columns (default) or switch devices like on Activity.
Kanban keeps the web board look; list stacks one status at a time and suits long task names.
Columns per screen on a phone. Two shows the whole board in two pages; tablets always show four.
One column is the classic list; two packs more tasks on screen.
All four statuses at a glance. Read-only — tap a card to open it.
Projects with more sessions come first in the chip row. When on, the manual order below is ignored.
Arranges the chip row left to right; new projects are appended at the end.
No session projects yet — long-press 全部 on the 动态 or 会话 tab to create one.
Add a description (or attach files) — the server rejects an empty prompt.
Create one to run a prompt on a schedule — e.g. a daily 09:00 standup report.
“%1$s” and its run history will be removed — the desktop side will no longer see it either.
Scheduled fires and manual runs will show up here.
This server version doesn\'t support automations yet.
Can\'t compute the next run — check the expression or timezone.
The server evaluates the schedule in this IANA timezone — the phone never converts times.
Source of truth: real session usage from the codeg server. Gateway-side cost lives in the zcode-hub panel — the two are complementary, never reconciled.
No devices in the current scope.
This server version doesn\'t support token usage yet.
The scan hit its row cap — numbers cover only the most recent slice.
%1$s in · %2$s out · %3$s cache read · %4$d turns · %5$d conversations
Gateway-side cost accounting lives in zcode-hub; this page and that panel are complementary and deliberately never reconciled.
This device\'s codeg build predates the import surface — upgrade it to import.
Sessions run by CLIs on that device will show up here, grouped by project folder.
Another %1$d session(s) carry no project path and are not listed.
